subject: history

moments.title: Planning Overlord
moments.body: Operation Overlord is planned over a year. Eisenhower (Supreme Commander) and Montgomery (ground commander) coordinate British, American, Canadian, Free French, Polish forces. Deception (Operation Fortitude) convinces German command the landing will be at Pas-de-Calais.
moments.takeaway: The Allies achieved a strategic surprise against an alerted enemy on a fortified coast — the largest amphibious operation in history.

moments.title: D-Day
moments.body: Five beaches — Utah, Omaha (US), Gold, Juno (Canadian), Sword (British) — plus airborne drops behind the lines. Omaha takes the worst casualties (around 2,400). By nightfall the Allies hold a beachhead. Within a week, around 326,000 troops are ashore.

quote.text: You are about to embark upon the Great Crusade, toward which we have striven these many months.
quote.attrib: Dwight Eisenhower, Order of the Day, 6 June 1944

moments.takeaway: Eisenhower drafted a statement taking sole responsibility if the landings failed. He kept it in his wallet for years afterwards.

moments.title: Breakout and Paris
moments.who: US, British, Canadian, Free French forces
moments.body: Operation Cobra (25 July) breaks the German lines. The Falaise pocket (12-21 August) traps and destroys two German armies. Paris is liberated 25 August. By December the Allies are at the German border.
moments.takeaway: The Western Front was opened. The Red Army, which had been doing most of the war's fighting, was about to enter Germany from the east.

now.title: Eighty years on
now.body: The 80th anniversary in 2024 was the last likely to be attended by significant numbers of D-Day veterans. War cemeteries at Bayeux, Colleville-sur-Mer, Ranville hold the dead. Antony Beevor and Max Hastings have produced the major modern English-language histories.
now.open_questions: Could D-Day have been earlier? Stalin had pushed for a second front since 1942. The 1942 Dieppe raid demonstrated the difficulty. The 1943 invasions of North Africa and Italy may have delayed Normandy by months, but also weakened Germany.

reflection: Logistics wins wars. D-Day was a triumph not primarily of valour (though there was plenty) but of preparation, deception, materiel, and coordinating multinational forces on a vast scale.
